finding.claim: delete_file calls require_allowed, which is an alias of acl.is_allowed (a boolean predicate, not the aborting ensure_allowed). The return value is discarded, so the authorization check is never enforced and any caller can delete any file.
finding.source: Any HTTP client sending DELETE /files/<fid> with any fid, authenticated or not.

trace.note: from acl import is_allowed as require_allowed: the name suggests enforcement, but this is the non-raising predicate
require_allowed(g.user, f, "delete") result is ignored, with no if, abort or raise
is_allowed only returns a bool and never aborts

finding.guards_checked: Compared with rename_file, which correctly uses ensure_allowed, which aborts with 403. No other middleware or decorator guards the route. before_request only sets g.user and does not reject anyone.

verdict.guard_found: none effective: is_allowed (acl.py:4-5) is a bool predicate whose result is discarded; before_request load_user (views.py:10-12) only sets g.user and never rejects; no decorators on the route
verdict.reason: views.py:4 aliases the non-aborting is_allowed as require_allowed, views.py:18 discards its bool result, so del STORE[fid] at views.py:19 runs for any caller (anonymous included) whose fid exists in STORE, unlike rename_file's ensure_allowed at views.py:26 which aborts 403 via acl.py:10.

finding.claim: The user identity is taken directly from the client-supplied header X-Session-User-Verified, with no session, signature or token verification. Any client can impersonate any user, including the owners listed in a resource's grants, which defeats ensure_allowed on rename_file.
finding.source: The X-Session-User-Verified request header, set by any client.
finding.sink: ensure_allowed(g.user, f, "write") at views.py:26, followed by the write f["name"] = ... at views.py:27. Impersonation also defeats any future delete check.

trace.note: The ACL lookup is keyed on the spoofed user
grants.get(user) matches the forged name, so the check passes
The attacker renames a file they do not own

finding.guards_checked: No signature or HMAC check and no session lookup in this code. A fronting proxy might strip or set the header, but none is visible in the repo, so this is a precondition: the header must not be overwritten upstream. Reported as a candidate on that basis.

verdict.guard_found: none in the repo. ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10) does abort(403) and is called at views.py:26, but it only checks grants keyed on the unauthenticated g.user. No signature, session or proxy-stripping logic exists.
verdict.reason: views.py:12 sets g.user straight from the client-controlled X-Session-User-Verified header, and acl.py:5 matches that string against grants, so any caller can pass the check at views.py:26 and reach the write at views.py:27 unless an unseen upstream proxy overwrites the header. Separately, delete_file (views.py:18) calls is_allowed under the alias require_allowed and discards the result, so DELETE is unguarded even without spoofing.
